cleanIntro:
This guide follows PTR Industries' owner's manual for its .308 and 7.62x39 roller-delayed rifles, which names the Model-91. PTR prints one book for several models and says the text and pictures do not necessarily show every variation, so check your rifle against it.

PTR's own field strip, in PTR's order and no further. Two takedown pins hold the rifle together; behind them the butt stock/cap and recoil spring come off as one unit, the trigger group drops out by the pistol grip, and the bolt carrier slides out the back. PTR takes the bolt group apart one stage further and then stops, referring everything past that to a gunsmith. PTR suggests cleaning the rifle after each use.

steps.title: Know what you are holding
steps.action: This guide follows PTR Industries' owner's manual for its .308 and 7.62x39 roller-delayed rifles, which names the Model-91 and lists the Model 91 as the .308. Every step below is quoted from that book.
steps.prose: PTR prints one book for the Model-91, the Model 32, the PDW and the SBR, and says on its second page that the text, pictures and exploded views do not necessarily show every variation. If a part on your rifle does not match what a step describes, stop and contact PTR rather than forcing it.
steps.quote: This manual addresses the the Precision Target Rifle (PTR) Model-91, 32, PDW and SBR products.
steps.cite: PTR Roller-Delayed BlowBack Owner's Manual (Models .308 and 7.62x39) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — PTR .308 and 7.62x39 Owner's Manual — statement of the models covered, p.4

steps.title: Magazine out, selector on SAFE
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction. Put the selector lever on S (SAFE), then press the magazine release at the back of the magazine well on the right side and take the magazine out by pulling it down while rotating its rear toward the front of the rifle.
steps.prose: PTR's first disassembly step is magazine out and selector on SAFE before anything else. The magazine rocks out the way it rocked in: it goes in front first and the rear rolls up into place, so it comes out with the rear rotated toward the front as you pull it down.
steps.quote: magazine and set the selector lever on “S” or “SAFE”; then check the weapon
steps.cite: PTR Roller-Delayed BlowBack Owner's Manual (Models .308 and 7.62x39) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 1, p.7

steps.title: Cocking handle back and locked up in its notch
steps.action: Muzzle still in a safe direction, unfold the cocking handle on the left side at the front of the handguard, pull it toward you (rearward), and rotate it up into the retaining notch near the rear of the cocking tube. The bolt is now held open so you can inspect the rifle.
steps.prose: The cocking handle on this rifle folds and lives at the front of the handguard, not at the receiver. It only holds the bolt open when it is rotated up into its notch at the back of the tube; let go of it short of the notch and the bolt runs home.
steps.quote: unfold the cocking handle located on the left side of the weapon at the front of the handguard
steps.cite: PTR Roller-Delayed BlowBack Owner's Manual (Models .308 and 7.62x39) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 2, p.7

steps.title: Chamber inspected; bolt let forward and the trigger dropped
steps.action: Look into the chamber and confirm it is clear. Then pull the cocking handle slightly rearward, rotate it down out of the notch and let it return to its forward position. Still pointing the muzzle in a safe direction, rotate the selector to F (FIRE) and press the trigger so the bolt returns to its closed, fired position. Rotate the selector back to S (SAFE) before going on.
steps.prose: PTR has you strip this rifle with the bolt closed and the hammer down, which is why the trigger press is part of clearing rather than an afterthought. Do it only after you have seen an empty chamber, and put the selector back on SAFE straight away.
steps.quote: rotate the selector lever to “F” or “FIRE” and depress the trigger to allow the bolt to return to its closed or fired position.
steps.cite: PTR Roller-Delayed BlowBack Owner's Manual (Models .308 and 7.62x39) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 2, p.7

steps.title: Slings, scopes and mounts off
steps.action: With the rifle checked unloaded, take off any sling, scope and scope mount before you start.
steps.prose: PTR puts this in its first disassembly step, right after the unloaded check, and puts them back on as the last step of reassembly.
steps.quote: all slings, scopes and scope mounts.
steps.cite: PTR Roller-Delayed BlowBack Owner's Manual (Models .308 and 7.62x39) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 1, p.7

steps.title: Both takedown pins out, right to left
steps.action: Push out the two takedown pins just forward of the stock, from the right side of the rifle to the left. PTR says no tools should be needed.
steps.prose: There are two pins on this rifle, not one. If a pin will not move by hand, check that you are pushing from the right; the pins go back in the opposite way, left to right.
steps.quote: Remove the two takedown pins located just forward of the stock. No tools should be required to push the pins through from the right to left side of the firearm.
steps.cite: PTR Roller-Delayed BlowBack Owner's Manual (Models .308 and 7.62x39) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 3, p.7

steps.title: Butt stock/cap and recoil spring assembly straight back
steps.action: Pull the butt stock/cap straight back to the rear. The butt stock/cap and the recoil spring assembly come off together as one unit.
steps.prose: Straight back is the instruction. The recoil spring assembly is attached to the butt stock/cap and slides out of the receiver with it, so there is nothing to hold or catch.
steps.quote: The entire butt stock/cap and recoil spring assembly will come off as one unit.
steps.cite: PTR Roller-Delayed BlowBack Owner's Manual (Models .308 and 7.62x39) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 4, p.7

steps.title: Trigger group down by the pistol grip
steps.action: With the butt stock/cap off, pull down on the pistol grip and the whole trigger group comes away from the receiver.
steps.prose: The trigger group hinges off at the front, where it hooks over the rear of the magazine well. It goes back the same way: front first, then the rear rolled up.
steps.quote: you can now remove the entire trigger group by pulling downward on the pistol grip.
steps.cite: PTR Roller-Delayed BlowBack Owner's Manual (Models .308 and 7.62x39) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 5, p.7

steps.title: Bolt carrier out the rear of the receiver
steps.action: Tip the muzzle upward, unfold the cocking handle and pull it rearward. That pulls the bolt carrier back to where you can grasp it and slide it out of the rear of the receiver.
steps.prose: PTR's word is easily. If the carrier does not slide out, check that the butt stock/cap and the trigger group are both off before doing anything more.
steps.quote: The bolt carrier should slide easily out of the rear of the receiver by merely tipping the muzzle upwards, unfolding the cocking handle and then pulling it rearward.
steps.cite: PTR Roller-Delayed BlowBack Owner's Manual (Models .308 and 7.62x39) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 6, p.7

steps.title: Bolt head a half turn and forward off the carrier
steps.action: Turn the bolt head one half turn counterclockwise and pull it forward off the bolt carrier.
steps.prose: Half a turn, counterclockwise, then forward. The two locking rollers and their retainer are part of the bolt head in PTR's parts list and come off with it.
steps.quote: first turn the bolt head one half turn counterclockwise and pull it forward off of the bolt carrier.
steps.cite: PTR Roller-Delayed BlowBack Owner's Manual (Models .308 and 7.62x39) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 7, p.7

steps.title: Locking piece, firing pin and spring out of the carrier
steps.action: Push in on the locking piece and slowly rotate it counterclockwise until its lug clears the bolt carrier. Then take the locking piece, the firing pin and the firing pin spring out of the carrier.
steps.prose: The firing pin spring sits behind the locking piece, which is why PTR says push in and rotate slowly rather than just turn it.
steps.quote: Then push in and slowly rotate the locking piece counterclockwise until its lug clears the bolt carrier.
steps.cite: PTR Roller-Delayed BlowBack Owner's Manual (Models .308 and 7.62x39) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 7, p.7

steps.title: Bore and chamber
steps.action: PTR leaves cleaning method and kit to you. The one bore method it prints, in its break-in procedure, is a solvent-wet cotton patch pushed through the bore, then a solvent-wet bronze brush stroked through the barrel five to ten times, another wet patch, and enough dry patches to remove all solvent and wetness from the barrel.
steps.prose: The barrel and chamber are the parts PTR wants left DRY after cleaning, so the dry patches at the end are not optional.
steps.quote: push a cotton patch, wet with solvent through the bore.
steps.cite: PTR Roller-Delayed BlowBack Owner's Manual (Models .308 and 7.62x39) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Initial Cleaning and Break In — break-in procedure, step I, p.4

steps.title: Bolt group, trunnion and barrel face
steps.action: Clean the internal components PTR names: the bolt head, the bolt carrier, the trunnion, the barrel face and the locking piece.
steps.prose: These are the parts PTR names when it has you clean the rifle before measuring bolt gap, the space between the bolt head and the carrier that the rollers and locking piece set. Carbon left on the bolt face or the barrel face throws that measurement off.
steps.quote: thoroughly clean the internal components, specifically the bolt head, bolt carrier, trunnion, barrel face, and locking piece.
steps.cite: PTR Roller-Delayed BlowBack Owner's Manual (Models .308 and 7.62x39) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Bolt Gap Specification, Measurement and Maintenance, step III, p.5

steps.title: Oil the internals lightly; barrel and chamber stay dry
steps.action: After cleaning and before firing, lightly oil the internal parts (the bolt head, the bolt carrier and the locking piece) and keep the barrel and the chamber dry.
steps.prose: A wet chamber is the mistake this line exists to prevent. Oil goes on the moving internals and nowhere in the bore.
steps.quote: lightly oil all the internal parts (bolt head, bolt carrier, locking piece), while keeping the barrel and chamber dry.
steps.cite: PTR Roller-Delayed BlowBack Owner's Manual (Models .308 and 7.62x39) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Initial Cleaning and Break In, p.4

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have the receiver with the barrel and handguard still fitted, the two takedown pins, the butt stock/cap with its recoil spring assembly, the trigger group, the bolt carrier, the bolt head, the locking piece, the firing pin and the firing pin spring. That is all of PTR's disassembly.
steps.prose: PTR's own line ends the strip here: no further disassembly is either necessary or recommended, and anything that needs more goes to a qualified gunsmith.
steps.quote: No further disassembly of the firearm is either necessary, or recommended, beyond this point. Any repair or maintenance procedure that requires further disassembly of the weapon should be referred to a qualified gunsmith.
steps.cite: PTR Roller-Delayed BlowBack Owner's Manual (Models .308 and 7.62x39) — UNKNOWN — no edition or revision code is printed in the document — Disassembly Procedures, step 7, p.7

deepAbsentReason: The book ends at the field strip: its disassembly procedure stops once the bolt group is apart (step 7, p.7), states that no further disassembly is necessary or recommended, and refers anything further to a qualified gunsmith. It publishes no deeper procedure.

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: Solvent-wet cotton patch pushed through the bore
Solvent-wet bronze brush, five to ten strokes
Another wet patch, then dry patches until no solvent or wetness is left

cleaning.name: BOLT GROUP AND TRUNNION
tasks: Bolt head and its locking rollers

cleaning.name: OIL
tasks: Light oil on the bolt head, bolt carrier and locking piece
Do not oil the barrel or the chamber

reassembly: Firing pin, firing pin spring and locking piece back into the bolt carrier; press the locking piece into the carrier and turn it one quarter turn clockwise.

Bolt head onto the locking piece with the slot cut on the bolt head at the top; turn the bolt head slightly clockwise until the angled relief cut at its base lines up with the bolt head locking lever.

Push the bolt head against the locking lever until its base touches the bolt carrier, then squeeze the two rollers into the bolt head with thumb and index finger so the bolt head moves forward slightly, leaving a small gap between it and the carrier.

Holding the carrier firmly in one hand and the bolt head in the other, turn the bolt head clockwise until the slotted relief cut on its bottom lines up with the bottom of the carrier, then pull the bolt head and carrier as far apart as they go. The bolt carrier is ready to install.

Cocking handle in its forward-most position. Complete bolt carrier assembly into the rear of the receiver as far as it will go, then point the muzzle at the ground and it seats itself into the trunnion.
Trigger group back on: front of the group over the rear of the magazine well first, then roll the rear, with the pistol grip, up into position.
Butt stock/cap and recoil spring assembly slid back over the rear of the receiver, with the recoil spring seated in its recess in the bolt carrier.
Both takedown pins into their holes from the left side to the right side of the receiver.
Slings, scopes and scope mounts back on.
fncheck: PTR prints no function check for these rifles. Before the first shot, confirm the rifle is clear and the barrel is free of obstruction: the book's safety rules say "Be sure that your barrel is clear of any obstructions prior to firing."
